motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing; all transitions and the facet entrance.

motion.name: facet-assemble
motion.value: per facet group: short translate along 45deg (6-8 drawing units) + opacity, 1100ms ease-out, stagger 60-480ms; edges at 640ms over 700ms; once
motion.purpose: Hero logo entrance; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion (facets at rest).

motion.name: rule-draw-nav
motion.value: transform scaleX 0 to 1 from left, 320ms ease-out
motion.purpose: Nav link hover/focus rule in the live line; stays drawn on the current section. Also the action arrow nudge (6px).

motion.name: rule-draw-entry
motion.value: transform scaleX 0 to 1 from left, 600ms ease-out
motion.purpose: Work entry hover rule in the live line.

motion.name: fill-state
motion.purpose: Copy button purple hover and lime copied state.

motion.name: copied-hold
motion.purpose: How long the copied (or failed) label stays before reverting.

motion.name: menu-cross
motion.value: outer lines translateY(+/-7px) rotate(+/-45deg), middle line opacity 0; 320ms ease-out (opacity 200ms)
motion.purpose: Phone menu button turning from three lines into an X on the 45-degree axis.

motion.name: menu-wipe
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0), 420ms ease-out, no fade; visibility flips after close
motion.purpose: Phone menu panel wiping down from the bar. Instant under reduced motion.

motion.name: card-recede
motion.purpose: Inactive work cards in the phone carousel; tick colour changes on the same timing. No transition under reduced motion.

motion.name: carousel-nudge
motion.value: translateX 0 to -48px at 40% and back, 1100ms ease-out, 300ms delay; once, when the track is 40% in view
motion.purpose: Shows the phone work row moves sideways. Skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: carousel-height
motion.value: track height set to the active card's offsetHeight, overflow-y hidden; height 420ms ease-out
motion.purpose: Phone work track follows the active card so short roles leave no empty space below. No transition under reduced motion; cleared on desktop.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Phone: menu button and full-screen panel, full-width work swipe carousel, inline stack groups with icons, 44px touch controls.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Tablet and below: big logo plane and contact facet drop behind the text at --mark-opacity.

dark.persistence: localStorage 'theme' (light|dark), try/catch; inline head script applies it before paint; no saved value = system preference

opacity.name: mark-opacity
opacity.purpose: Group opacity of the big logo plane and the contact facet when they sit behind the text at 1080px and below. Deliberate exception to the Flat Plane Rule; never applied to a surface.

narrative.northStar: The Concert Poster for Shipped Work
narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Concert Poster for Shipped Work"**

The site is a Zürich-school typographic poster. By default it is printed on warm paper; in dark mode the same poster is printed on neutral black, so the logo, the purple, and the lime are the only colour on the page. Its only image is the brand mark itself: the real logo, enlarged to poster scale, a violet square on its point cut into an indigo facet, an aubergine facet, and white slivers, outlined in near-black. Everything else is one heavy grotesk set flush-left, ragged-right, on a strict 12-column grid, separated by straight 2px rules. Work is billed like acts on a poster: the bigger the shipped system, the bigger its name.

Density is generous and rhythmic, not airy. Distances come from one 8px module (the facet unit). Two colours speak. The logo's purple is the main highlight, spent on what has to read clearly: the action, the key figures, the bullets. Lime is the second brand colour, and it means one thing: live. It marks availability, the section you are in, the entry under the pointer, keyboard focus, and a confirmed copy. Depth does not exist: no shadows, no radius, no translucent layers; on tablets and phones the big marks drop behind the text as faint watermarks, the one sanctioned use of group opacity. State is drawn with line: a broken rule is past work, a solid lime rule is live or current, a solid purple rule is the action.

The world refuses the developer-template furniture (avatar, tagline, logo-chip grid, card rows) and its terminal clichés (monospace, prompts, blinking cursors, green text on black).
keyCharacteristics: Light by default on warm white and beige paper; dark theme on neutral black and grey grounds, by system preference or by the header switch.
One typeface (Archivo Variable), varied by width axis rather than by a second family.
One module (8px), one grid (12 columns), one angle (45°).
Purple is the main highlight; lime marks live state only, as fill or line, never as text.
Straight lines only: rules, dashes, squares, square-capped arrows, diamond facets.
Flat planes; zero radius; zero shadow. At 1080px and below the big marks become watermarks behind the text.
Bilingual: Spanish at `/`, English at `/en/`, same composition.

rules.name: The Paper Ground Rule
rules.body: In the light theme, grounds are warm white or beige, nothing else. Purple and lime appear as small fills, lines, and type, or as a facet plane; neither ever becomes a section background.

rules.name: The Neutral Night Rule
rules.body: The dark theme's grounds and inks are neutral black and greys with no hue; the logo, the purple, and the lime are the only colour on a dark page. Never tint a dark ground or ink toward violet or aubergine, and never use the violet or the indigo as a ground. Every dark value is a reassignment of an existing custom property; components never branch on theme.

rules.name: The Clear Purple Rule
rules.body: Purple is the main highlight: what you can act on and the figures that carry the argument. If an element is neither, it wears ink.

rules.name: The Live Rule
rules.body: Lime means live, and only live: available now, the section on screen, the thing under the pointer or the keyboard, the copy that just succeeded. It is a fill (`live`) or a line (`live-ink`), never running text, never a section ground.

rules.name: The Logo-Plus-Lime Rule
rules.body: Every hue comes from the logo's facets or is a tint of the same aubergine (the light theme's inks), plus the one lime. The grounds and the dark theme's neutral greys are the only other colours. Technology marks never bring their brand colours; they take the text colour (`currentColor`) in both themes.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Archivo Variable is the only family. Contrast is made with the width axis (75 / 100 / 125) and weight, never with a second typeface or a monospace.

rules.name: The Billing Rule
rules.body: A work entry's title size is set by how much of the system was shipped (weight 3, 2, 1), not by recency.

rules.name: The Flat Plane Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. Surfaces differ only by flat fill and are separated only by rules. One deliberate exception, chosen by the user: at 1080px and below the big marks (hero logo, contact facet) sit behind the text at Mark Opacity, as group opacity on the whole mark, never as a translucent panel or a tint on a surface. At 1081px and up they stay full-colour planes beside the text.

rules.name: The State-by-Line Rule
rules.body: A broken rule means past or archived; a solid lime rule means live or current; a solid purple rule means the action. Links and entries draw their lime rule in from the left on hover; the current nav section keeps it. Only the square controls (language switch, theme switch, copy button, carousel steps) fill: purple on hover, lime when copying succeeds.

rules.name: The One Angle Rule
rules.body: 45° is the only diagonal. Everything else is horizontal or vertical.

dos: Do derive every distance from the 8px module and place every block on the 12-column grid.
Do set every light section on warm white (#fbf9f5) or beige (#f2ede4) paper, and every dark section on neutral black (#121212) or grey (#1c1c1c).
Do add new colours as custom properties with a value for each theme; components read the property and never branch on theme.
Do separate content with straight 2px rules; use 1px quiet rules only to subdivide inside a block.
Do draw state with line: dashed for past work, solid lime for live or current, purple for the action.
Do spend the brand purple on what must read clearly: actions, key figures, bullets, the caret.
Do spend lime only on live state: availability, the current section, hover and focus, a confirmed copy.
Do set new hierarchy with Archivo's width axis (125 for section heads, 75 for figures) before adding size.
Do build any new image from the logo's construction as flat facet planes on 45°.
Do set a big mark behind text only at 1080px and below, as group opacity at `--mark-opacity` with the text above it; at desktop widths keep it full colour beside the text.
Do give every motion a reduced-motion state that shows the end frame at rest.
Do give every phone touch control a 44px square hit area.
Do ship every surface in Spanish at `/` and English at `/en/` with the same composition.
donts: Don't fill a section ground with the violet, the indigo, or lime; in dark mode the ground is neutral black or grey only, never tinted toward violet or aubergine.
Don't set running body text in purple; body is soft ink.
Don't set any text in lime; lime is a fill or a line, and text on a lime fill is dark aubergine.
Don't use lime for emphasis that isn't live state; emphasis is purple.
Don't round corners, add shadows, or use translucent glass layers; the Mark Opacity watermark is the only opacity on a mark, and it never applies to a surface.
Don't wrap content in cards or set labels and tags as pills.
Don't use colour gradients; the only linear-gradient allowed is the hard-stop dash pattern that draws a broken rule.
Don't add a second typeface, a monospace, or terminal devices (prompts, blinking cursors, green text on black).
Don't introduce any hue outside the logo's facets, their aubergine tints, the one lime, and the grounds.
Don't put small uppercase labels (eyebrows) above headings; a heading stands on its own rule.
Don't mark live state with a dot or a circle; the live marker is a square.
Don't use any diagonal other than 45°, or curved lines, in the world's own drawing; published technology marks keep their own shapes.
Don't give a technology mark its brand colour or a chip; it is a 16px `currentColor` mark beside its name.
